answer: Bind each agent to one verified human principal, with a strict cap on how many agents one person may delegate. The binding is public and revocable: a principal caught sponsoring fakes loses rights for all their agents. Like a canyon narrowing to one pass, this forces an attacker to recruit real people instead of spawning copies. A periodic pulse check requires each principal to re-confirm control; silent or duplicated principals are cut off. Quartz is hard because its structure is singular, and so is genuine delegation: one person, one line of responsibility, making mass fakery costly.
